title: DeadDropResource does not speak RFC 8428 SenML+CBOR
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: correctness (security impact on privacy)

Spec 18.9 and get_link_description advertise Content-Format 112
(application/senml+cbor). RFC 8428 Table 4 uses integer labels
(0=n, 2=v, 3=vs, -2=bn, ...). lichen.senml.codec.pack() emits those
labels. ConfessionsResource correctly uses unpack().

DeadDrop POST uses _decode_single_cbor() plus _senml_text() /
_extract_ttl() which look up string keys "n", "vs", "v" on each
record. GET /deaddrop wraps metadata as string-key maps and labels
the body ct=112.

Evidence with pack() of privacy=private, ttl=3600, type=message:
- _senml_text(payload, "privacy") is None
- _extract_ttl returns 86400
- stored privacy is "public"
- unauthenticated GET lists the drop
- unpack() of the GET body returns SenmlRecord objects with all
  fields None (string labels without trailing _ are ignored)

Oracle tests hide this by cbor2.dumps()'ing Python dicts with
string keys, which is not RFC 8428 SenML+CBOR.

Impact: spec-compliant C/Rust/Python pack() peers cannot set TTL,
type, recipient, or privacy. "private"/"group" drops are stored
public (confidentiality failure). GET bodies are not SenML+CBOR
so cross-impl interop fails spec 18.9 "MUST produce identical
SenML output".

Acceptance: POST of lichen.senml.codec.pack() records honors ttl,
type, recipient, and privacy; private drops are omitted from public
GET and return 4.03 by id; GET collection unpack()s to records
with n/vs/v populated.
close_reason: DeadDrop POST/GET speak RFC 8428 integer-label SenML+CBOR via lichen.senml.codec (pack GET, SenmlRecord.from_cbor_map POST). pack() privacy/ttl/type/recipient honored; private omitted from public GET and 4.03 by id; collection GET unpacks with n/vs/v. Independent tests in test_deaddrop_resource.py (hand-built Table 4 maps + pack/unpack). 46 passed.
